databaselibraryreadingslab

escargo (working title) turns the dome into an audiovisual instrument the audience can interact with.

It allows easy integration with other experiences (everything from interactive formations to collectively collaborative performances to participatory VJ sets to between show activities) using technology people already have (phones) and no additional hardware setup (the websocket runs on existing machines) with interactions that a) make the dome feel legible and tactile for audiences and b) allow easy measurement of audience response in realtime for research purposes (including creative interactions and actual polling/feedback).

Phone. Audience moves and touches their phone to interact.

Hub. Keeps track of and routes actions, writes a log.

AV Engine. Drives audio visual output rendered in realtime on the dome based on actions.

Artist. Manages available actions, objects, and contextual elements to create unified experience.

Demo

How can we make it legible to audiences as a surface, space, and audiovisual tool?

How can we give audiences agency to engage with it?
